rules.rule: Minimum end distance e1 (parallel to load direction)
rules.source_quote: End distance e1 ≥ 1.2d0 (Table 3.3 minimum)

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance e2 (perpendicular to load direction)
rules.source_quote: Edge distance e2 ≥ 1.2d0 (Table 3.3 minimum); NOTE: pre-2005 ENV draft gave 1.5d0 — that value is superseded

rules.rule: Minimum slotted-hole distances e3 and e4 (to slot centre)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.3: e3 (end of slot) ≥ 1.5d0; e4 (edge to slot centre) ≥ 1.5d0

rules.rule: Minimum bolt pitch p1 (in direction of load)
rules.source_quote: Spacing p1 ≥ 2.2d0 (Table 3.3 minimum)

rules.rule: Minimum bolt pitch p2 (perpendicular to load direction)
rules.source_quote: Spacing p2 ≥ 2.4d0 (Table 3.3 minimum)

rules.rule: Maximum edge distance e1, e2 — member exposed to weather or corrosion
rules.units: mm (t = thickness of thinner outer connected part)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.3 maximum: e1, e2 ≤ 4t + 40 mm (exposed to weather / corrosion)

rules.rule: Maximum edge distance e1, e2 — member not exposed to weather
rules.units: mm (t = thickness of thinner outer connected part)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.3 maximum: e1, e2 ≤ max(8t, 125 mm) for non-exposed members

rules.rule: Maximum bolt pitch p1, p2 (standard, tension or shear members)
rules.units: mm (t = thickness of thinner outer connected part)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.3 maximum: p1, p2 ≤ min(14t, 200 mm)

rules.rule: Maximum pitch p1 for inner bolt rows in compression direction
rules.value: smaller of 28t or 400 mm (single free-source; verify against EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.3)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.3 compression-member inner rows: p1,i ≤ min(28t, 400 mm); outer rows: min(14t, 200 mm)

rules.rule: Bearing-resistance un-reduced threshold — end distance e1
rules.value: e1 ≥ 1.5·d0 (below this, αd bearing factor reduces; see bolt-shear-and-bearing)
rules.source_quote: Table 3.4: for bearing not to be reduced, e1 ≥ 1.5d0 (entering the αd formula)

rules.rule: Bearing-resistance un-reduced threshold — pitch p1
rules.source_quote: Table 3.4: for bearing not to be reduced, p1 ≥ 3.75d0

rules.rule: Standard round-hole clearance — M12 and M14 bolts
rules.value: +1 mm (d0 = 13 mm for M12; 15 mm for M14)
rules.source_quote: M12, M14: clearance = 1 mm (d0 = d + 1 mm); note: commonly mis-stated as +2 mm

rules.rule: Standard round-hole clearance — M16 to M24 bolts
rules.source_quote: M16, M18, M20, M22, M24: clearance = 2 mm (d0 = d + 2 mm)

rules.rule: Standard round-hole clearance — M27 and larger bolts
rules.source_quote: M27 and larger: clearance = 3 mm (d0 = d + 3 mm)

rules.rule: P358 practical hole clearance convention (standardised connections)
rules.value: d + 2 mm for d ≤ 24 mm; d + 3 mm for d > 24 mm; holding-down (HD) bolts d + 6 mm
rules.source_quote: P358: standard holes d + 2 mm (d ≤ 24 mm), d + 3 mm (d > 24 mm); HD bolts d + 6 mm. Note: for M12/M14 use EN +1 mm, not P358's +2 mm

rules.rule: Design preload of a preloaded bolt Fp,C
rules.units: kN (fub = bolt tensile strength N/mm², As = tensile stress area mm²)
rules.source_quote: P358 §6 Check 4: Fp,C = 0.7 fub As; preloaded assemblies are property class 8.8 or 10.9 to BS EN 14399

rules.rule: Design slip resistance of one preloaded bolt Fs,Rd
rules.source_quote: P358 §6 Check 4: Fs,Rd = (ks · n · μ / γM3) · Fp,C

rules.rule: Hole shape factor ks — standard clearance holes
rules.source_quote: Table 3.6: ks = 1.0 for fasteners in standard clearance holes; reduced for oversized or slotted holes

rules.rule: Slip factor μ — Class A faying surface (blasted, loose rust removed, not pitted)
rules.source_quote: EN 1090-2 Table 18 Class A: blasted, loose rust removed, not pitted → μ = 0.5

rules.rule: Slip factor μ — Class B (blasted + alkali-zinc-silicate or metallised coating)
rules.source_quote: EN 1090-2 Table 18 Class B: blast-cleaned + alkali-zinc-silicate or thermally sprayed metal → μ = 0.4

rules.rule: Slip factor μ — Class C (wire-brushed or flame-cleaned)
rules.source_quote: EN 1090-2 Table 18 Class C: wire-brushed or flame-cleaned → μ = 0.3

rules.rule: Slip factor μ — Class D (as-rolled / untreated)
rules.source_quote: EN 1090-2 Table 18 Class D: as-rolled → μ = 0.2

rules.rule: Partial factor γM0 — cross-section resistance (UK NA)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-1 (SCI P358 §1.6)
rules.source_quote: P358 §1.6 Major symbols: γM0 = 1.0 (UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-1)

rules.rule: Partial factor γM1 — member resistance to instability (UK NA)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-1 (SCI P358 §1.6)

rules.rule: Partial factor γM2 — bolts, welds, pins, plates in bearing (UK NA)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-8 (SCI P358 §1.6)
rules.source_quote: P358 §1.6: γM2 = 1.25 for connectors (UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-8); WATCH: a different γM2 = 1.1 applies to member net-section fracture

rules.rule: Partial factor γM2 — net-section fracture of a member in tension (UK NA)
rules.value: 1.1 (applied with fu, not fy; this is a MEMBER check, not a connector check)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-1 (SCI P358 §1.6)
rules.source_quote: P358 §1.6: γM2 = 1.1 for net-section fracture (UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-1); use with fu for member tension failure — distinct from the 1.25 connector value

rules.rule: Partial factor γM3 — slip resistance at ULS (UK NA)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-8 (SCI P358 §1.6)
rules.source_quote: P358 §1.6: γM3 = 1.25 at ULS for slip resistance (UK NA)

rules.rule: Partial factor γM3,ser — slip resistance at serviceability (UK NA)
rules.citation: UK NA to BS EN 1993-1-8 (SCI P358 §1.6)
rules.source_quote: P358 §1.6: γM3,ser = 1.10 at SLS for slip resistance (UK NA)

rules.rule: Effective throat — fillet weld
rules.value: a = 0.7 · s (a = throat, s = leg length)
rules.source_quote: P358 §7: a = 0.7s (throat = 0.7 × leg for equal-leg fillet)

rules.rule: P358 tabulated fillet weld design strength — S275 steel, longitudinal shear
rules.source_quote: P358 Table G.37: S275 longitudinal design strength fvw,d = 223 N/mm²

rules.rule: P358 tabulated fillet weld design strength — S275 steel, transverse
rules.source_quote: P358 Table G.37: S275 transverse design strength = 273 N/mm²

rules.rule: P358 tabulated fillet weld design strength — S355 steel, longitudinal shear
rules.source_quote: P358 Table G.37: S355 longitudinal design strength fvw,d = 241 N/mm²

rules.rule: P358 tabulated fillet weld design strength — S355 steel, transverse
rules.source_quote: P358 Table G.37: S355 transverse design strength = 295 N/mm²

rules.rule: Correlation factor βw — S275 steel
Correlation factor βw — S355 steel
P358 full-strength web weld throat — end-plate, S275 steel
rules.source_quote: P358 Appendix C: end-plate web weld → a ≥ 0.40tw (S275)

rules.rule: P358 full-strength web weld throat — end-plate, S355 steel
rules.source_quote: P358 Appendix C: end-plate web weld → a ≥ 0.48tw (S355)

rules.rule: S275 yield strength fy — thickness t ≤ 16 mm
rules.source_quote: S275: fy = 275 N/mm² for t ≤ 16 mm per EN 10025-2

rules.rule: S275 yield strength fy — thickness 16 mm < t ≤ 40 mm
rules.source_quote: S275: fy = 265 N/mm² for 16 < t ≤ 40 mm

rules.rule: S275 ultimate tensile strength fu (design value up to 100 mm)
rules.source_quote: S275: nominal fu = 410 N/mm² used for design calculations up to 100 mm thickness

rules.rule: S355 yield strength fy — thickness t ≤ 16 mm
rules.source_quote: S355: fy = 355 N/mm² for t ≤ 16 mm per EN 10025-2

rules.rule: S355 yield strength fy — thickness 16 mm < t ≤ 40 mm
rules.source_quote: S355: fy = 345 N/mm² for 16 < t ≤ 40 mm

rules.rule: S355 yield strength fy — thickness 40 mm < t ≤ 63 mm
rules.source_quote: S355: fy = 335 N/mm² for 40 < t ≤ 63 mm

rules.rule: S355 yield strength fy — thickness 63 mm < t ≤ 80 mm
rules.source_quote: S355: fy = 325 N/mm² for 63 < t ≤ 80 mm

rules.rule: S355 ultimate tensile strength fu (design value up to 100 mm)
rules.source_quote: S355: nominal fu = 470 N/mm² used for design calculations up to 100 mm thickness

rules.rule: Charpy impact toughness — subgrade JR
rules.source_quote: Subgrade JR: minimum 27 J Charpy V-notch at +20 °C

rules.rule: Charpy impact toughness — subgrade J0
rules.source_quote: Subgrade J0: minimum 27 J at 0 °C

rules.rule: Charpy impact toughness — subgrade J2
rules.source_quote: Subgrade J2: minimum 27 J at −20 °C

rules.rule: Charpy impact toughness — subgrade K2
rules.source_quote: Subgrade K2: minimum 40 J at −20 °C (K2 is more stringent than J2 at the same temperature)
